overview.en: Max Planck was a German physicist who originated quantum theory by introducing the concept of energy quanta to explain blackbody radiation. His revolutionary insight that energy is emitted in discrete packets marked the birth of modern physics.

early_life.en: Born in Kiel, Germany, Planck came from an academic family. He studied at the Universities of Munich and Berlin under Kirchhoff and Helmholtz, initially focusing on thermodynamics before turning his attention to the problem of blackbody radiation.

impact.en: Planck's quantum hypothesis fundamentally changed physics by revealing that energy at the atomic scale comes in discrete units. His constant, h, is one of the most fundamental constants in nature, and his work opened the door to quantum mechanics, one of the pillars of modern physics.

event.en: Earned his PhD from the University of Munich with a thesis on the second law of thermodynamics.
Became professor at the University of Berlin.
Introduced the quantum hypothesis to solve the blackbody radiation problem.
Awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of energy quanta.
Became president of the Kaiser Wilhelm Society (later Max Planck Society).

title.en: On the Law of Distribution of Energy in the Normal Spectrum

description.en: The paper introducing the quantum hypothesis and Planck's constant to explain blackbody radiation.
Comprehensive treatise on radiation theory incorporating quantum concepts.
Multi-volume textbook series covering the major branches of theoretical physics.

text.en: A new scientific truth does not triumph by convincing its opponents and making them see the light, but rather because its opponents eventually die, and a new generation grows up that is familiar with it.
Science cannot solve the ultimate mystery of nature because we ourselves are part of the mystery that we are trying to solve.
